The proposed metas "AI · RAG · agents" and "Event-driven · WebSockets" are drawn from the owner brief, not copied from TechMatrix. index.css: the hue tokens are at lines 45-50; the "a hue names a domain" comment is at lines 37-44.
survivors.recommendation: Keep the recommendation, with three implementation notes so it does not break the component or contradict a sibling section: (1) buildCompact() at SystemGraph.tsx:141 hard-codes ["laravel","ai","node","python","asterisk","realtime"] with a non-null NODES.find(...)! — if the "ai" and "realtime" ids are folded away, update that list (e.g. ["laravel","python","node","redis","asterisk","automation"]) or the compact layout will crash on undefined def.id; also update the role="img" aria-label at :211 and the "ten nodes" header comment at :30. (2) Add a hue field to NodeDef and drive the resting stroke/dot from hsl(var(--hue-backend)) for Laravel/Redis/APIs, hsl(var(--hue-realtime)) for Node.js/Asterisk, hsl(var(--hue-ai)) for Python, hsl(var(--hue-automation)) for Automation, hsl(var(--hue-cloud)) for Docker, keeping --primary for the hover state only (index.css says --primary is never reassigned). (3) TechMatrix.tsx currently files Node.js under the Backend group; per the brief (REAL-TIME: Node.js, TypeScript, WebSockets) move it to the "realtime" group so the hue mapping is consistent between the hero graph and the stack matrix.
survivors.why_it_matters: The visual contradicts the copy: the lead says Laravel first, the diagram says ten peers. This is the single biggest reason the 5-second read drifts from 'Laravel systems engineer' to 'generic full-stack'. Verdict today: Laravel reads primary in text only; Node.js has no obvious role ('tooling'); Python reads as scripting, not AI/data.

Rename the Insights title so 'engineering log' is used once, for TrackRecord.

survivors.title: On a 390px phone the reader scrolls two-plus viewports of hero (two 52px pills, CV link, 2×2 telemetry, a 516px-tall graph) before any proof, and the compact graph still shows Python and AI as separate peers

Fix the Suspense fallback aspect to the compact ratio so the graph does not jump.

survivors.title: Eight-question map: 'who' and 'how he thinks' are strong; 'what hard systems' is strong but late; 'why trust' is answered with the wrong currency; 'Node/Python role' is missing
survivors.evidence: src/components/TechMatrix.tsx:33 — `{ name: "Node.js", uses: ["Socket services", "Edge functions", "Tooling"] }` sits inside the "Backend" group (lines 23-35); there is no REAL-TIME group containing Node.js/TypeScript (TypeScript is under "Interface" at line 91), and Python appears nowhere in TechMatrix.tsx or ServiceExplorer.tsx:31-148. Hero lead paragraph runs to Hero.tsx:93, not 92. The "View Code → #" path is src/pages/ProjectDetail.tsx:91-93 with src/data/projects.ts githubUrl: "#" at lines 28, 77, 126, 175, 220, 265, 310, 361, 408.
survivors.recommendation: The fixes above, in priority order for this lens: (1) reorder so Audience + CaseStudies precede services; (2) swap marketplace stats for linked proof; (3) rebuild /projects and /project/:id from existing data; (4) give Node.js and Python explicit roles in the graph, services and stack; (5) unify the CTA label and kill the FAQ/chatbot contradictions. Nothing else needs rewriting.
survivors.why_it_matters: Timeline verdict: 5s — 'serious backend, Laravel' (good) but the diagram says 'ten technologies'; 20s — 'freelancer with earnings and a services menu' (the drop-off); 60s — 'he genuinely designs systems' (recovered by dossiers + principles); 2min — 'I'd take the call, but I clicked View Code and got #'. The page earns trust in the middle and loses it at the edges.

survivors.section: Site-wide (Hero, Navbar, Footer, Contact, Audience, Services, ServiceDetail, BlogPost, Checklist, NotFound, AIChatbot, CommandMenu, HireMe)
survivors.title: One dominant action is spelled 14 different ways across the site
survivors.evidence: Hero.tsx:105 "Book an Architecture Call"; Navbar.tsx:199 "Book a call" (640–1023px); Footer.tsx:9 `{ label: "Book a call", to: "/book" }`; CommandMenu.tsx:117 "Book an architecture call"; Audience.tsx:123 "Talk through this"; Contact.tsx:146 "Pick a time instead"; Contact.tsx:174 "Book a call now"; Contact.tsx:334 "Open full booking page"; Services.tsx:103 "Book a consultation"; ServiceDetail.tsx:91 "Book a free consultation"; ServiceDetail.tsx:173 "Book a consultation"; BlogPost.tsx:296 "Book a free call"; Checklist.tsx:194 "Book a free review"; NotFound.tsx:88 "Book a free 30-min call"; AIChatbot.tsx:427 "Book a free 15-min intro call →"; HireMe.tsx:26 "Hire Me"; CalendlyEmbed.tsx:17 `title = "Book a free 30-minute consultation"`

survivors.why_it_matters: A visitor who has read "Book an Architecture Call" three times and then meets "Book a consultation" or "Hire Me" is being sold a different, cheaper-sounding product at the moment of decision.

survivors.title: The destination page never says "Architecture Call" — scent breaks on arrival

Keep the three pills ("30 minutes", "Pick a time that works for you", "NDA-friendly") — they are good objection handling.
survivors.why_it_matters: Every primary CTA on the site promises an architecture call; the page that must close the 2-minute journey re-labels it as a generic free consultation, which is the freelance-marketplace framing the brief forbids.

survivors.section: Book page FAQ + Engagements + Contact form
survivors.title: Three different price floors and a "hire a developer" question on the booking page
survivors.evidence: Index.tsx JSON-LD cite lacked line numbers: src/pages/Index.tsx:59-66 `"@type": "Offer", name: "Sprint", ... priceSpecification: { "@type": "PriceSpecification", minPrice: "1500", priceCurrency: "USD"`. Rewrite the FAQ question as "What does an engagement cost?" and answer with the Sprint/Build/Scale shapes. Align the Contact budget buckets to the same floors ("Under $1,500" or drop the lowest bucket).
survivors.why_it_matters: A buyer who reads $1,500 on the home page and $2,500 on the booking page assumes one of them is a bait number; "hire a senior Laravel developer" is marketplace vocabulary on the page that should feel like an architecture discussion.

survivors.section: Projects page + ProjectDetail page closing CTA (HireMe)
survivors.title: The case-study route ends in "Hire Me" + "Back to Home" with forbidden marketing copy
survivors.evidence: ProjectDetail.tsx:290-300 is two <Button variant="outline"> links (line 292 "View All Projects" to /projects, line 297 "Back to Home" to /) followed by <HireMe /> at line 300, which itself renders a third button (HireMe.tsx:19-27, variant="outline-white", label "Hire Me") — not "three outline buttons then <HireMe />". Drop "Back to Home" (the Navbar logo does that). On ProjectDetail keep one ghost secondary "Explore Case Studies →" to /projects.
survivors.why_it_matters: This is the exit of the brief's L3 proof step; the strongest evidence on the site hands off to the weakest, most marketplace-flavoured CTA and the exact copy the brief lists as banned.

survivors.title: Case-study pages render dead "Live Demo" and "View Code" buttons pointing at "#"
survivors.evidence: ProjectDetail.tsx:84-89 `Live Demo` and :90-95 `View Code` rendered unconditionally; src/data/projects.ts:28,77,126,175,220,265,310,361,408 `githubUrl: "#"` (all nine) and :27,76,125 `liveUrl: "#"` (ids 1–3)

survivors.why_it_matters: Two prominent buttons that open a blank tab on the page meant to prove engineering rigour is the fastest way to lose the "senior engineer" impression.

survivors.title: Every secondary CTA sends visitors to a /projects grid whose cards open the wrong case study
survivors.evidence: Minor precision only: src/pages/Projects.tsx:223 reads `<Link key={project.id} to={`/project/${project.id}`}>` (the finding's quote omits the key prop). src/data/projects.ts top-level keys are at lines 2, 51, 100, 149, 198, 243, 288, 333, 384 (keys 1-9); key 5 at line 198-200 is "Focus Interiors, AI-Enhanced E-Commerce", which is the entry the "Focus Interiors" card should open.

Fix Projects.tsx to iterate `projectsData` (or `caseStudies`) so ids match.
survivors.why_it_matters: The 20-second "he has worked on systems like mine" step depends on the secondary CTA; today it lands on a card that opens a different project, which reads as carelessness.

survivors.section: Secondary CTA labels (Hero, Navbar, CaseStudies, CommandMenu, ServiceDetail, ProjectDetail, Footer)
survivors.title: Seven labels for the secondary action; none is the brief's "Explore Case Studies →"
survivors.evidence: Hero.tsx:108 "View Selected Work"; Navbar.tsx:261 "View all projects"; CaseStudies.tsx:216 "Browse all projects"; CommandMenu.tsx:118 `label: "All projects"`; ServiceDetail.tsx:96 "See related work"; ProjectDetail.tsx:292 "View All Projects"; Footer.tsx:6 `{ label: "Work", to: "/projects" }`
survivors.recommendation: Use "Explore Case Studies" (with the CTA primitive's `arrow` prop) for Hero, the Navbar mobile sheet, the CaseStudies footer CTA and ServiceDetail; use "Case studies" for the Footer sitemap entry and the CommandMenu page entry. There is currently no CTA constant in src/data/site.ts — add `export const CTA_PRIMARY = "Book an Architecture Call"` and `export const CTA_SECONDARY = "Explore Case Studies"` there (alongside OWNER/SOCIALS/CV_URL) and import them in the seven files, so the label lives in one place. Note ProjectDetail.tsx and ServiceDetail.tsx still use the old shadcn `Button` + `Link` pattern (and ServiceDetail's primary reads "Book a free consultation"); switch both to the `CTA` primitive when relabelling.
survivors.why_it_matters: The brief names exactly two CTAs; a visitor should recognise the secondary path by its wording from any section.

survivors.title: Two closing sections stacked back-to-back, each with a booking CTA and a WhatsApp CTA
survivors.evidence: Index.tsx:140-141 `<FinalCTA />` then `<Contact />`; FinalCTA.tsx:64 "Book an Architecture Call" + FinalCTA.tsx:66-77 `<CTA href={WHATSAPP_URL} tone="ghost" size="lg" arrow>...WhatsApp</CTA>`; Contact.tsx:145-147 "Pick a time instead", :148-153 "Chat on WhatsApp", :333-335 "Open full booking page", :342 `<CalendlyEmbed height={680} />`
survivors.recommendation: Keep FinalCTA as the single primary close (it has the best copy on the site) but drop its WhatsApp ghost button — WhatsApp already lives in Contact's channel list (Contact.tsx:34). In Contact, remove "Pick a time instead" and "Open full booking page" (FinalCTA 200px above already offers the call) so the section is one form plus one calendar.
survivors.why_it_matters: The brief asks to reduce repeated CTAs; two adjacent sections offering the same two channels four ways splits attention exactly where the decision is being made.

survivors.title: Inside Contact the primary action is ambiguous: form vs Calendly vs WhatsApp vs /book
survivors.evidence: Contact.tsx:145-147 `<CTA to="/book" tone="ghost" size="sm" arrow>Pick a time instead</CTA>` (rendered before the form); Contact.tsx:148-153 `<CTA href={WHATSAPP_URL} tone="quiet" size="sm">...Chat on WhatsApp`; Contact.tsx:294 `Send project brief` (the only solid `bg-primary` button in the section, :285); Contact.tsx:328-330 `Or book directly` / `Pick a slot for a free 30-minute architecture call.`; Contact.tsx:342 inline Calendly (loads assets.calendly.com widget.js on the home page)
survivors.recommendation: Decide that the written brief is Contact's job and the call is /book's job. Keep the form as the section's primary, keep the Email/WhatsApp channel rows, delete the inline `<CalendlyEmbed>` block (Contact.tsx:323-345) and the "Pick a time instead" CTA; the sent-state "Book a call now" (Contact.tsx:173-175) is the right moment for the call and should read "Book an Architecture Call". This also removes a third-party script from the landing page.
survivors.why_it_matters: Four routes with no visual ranking make the visitor choose a channel instead of taking the action; the brief wants one dominant action and whitespace.

survivors.title: The chatbot gates on a lead form, routes bookings to a 15-min WhatsApp call, and describes a different person
survivors.evidence: AIChatbot.tsx:249 `Ask my AI`; AIChatbot.tsx:298 `Before we start`, :299-301 `Quick intro so Usama can follow up if needed.`, :342 `Start chatting`; AIChatbot.tsx:420 `href="https://wa.me/923038004684?text=...book%20a%2015-min%20intro%20call"`, :427 `Book a free 15-min intro call →`; supabase/functions/chat/index.ts:29 `Usama Munawar is an AI Engineer & Full Stack Developer with 5+ years experience.`, :34 `Machine Learning & Deep Learning (TensorFlow, PyTorch, Hugging Face)`, :43 `Be enthusiastic about AI. If asked about pricing, suggest they reach out directly via the contact form, email, or WhatsApp.`; AIChatbot.tsx:226-234 launcher is `fixed bottom-4 right-4` — the only persistent CTA on <640px viewports where the Navbar CTA is `hidden sm:inline-flex` (Navbar.tsx:195)
survivors.recommendation: Remove `<AIChatbot />` from Index.tsx (its only mount). If the owner insists on keeping it: delete the lead gate, change the booking link to `<Link to="/book">Book an Architecture Call</Link>`, drop "Be enthusiastic about AI", and generate the system prompt from src/data/site.ts + services.ts so it says "Backend Systems Engineer" and the real stack.
survivors.why_it_matters: On phones the site's one always-visible button is "Ask my AI", which asks for name and phone before answering and then sells a shorter, different call — while the model behind it introduces Usama as an AI/full-stack developer, the exact impression the brief says to avoid.

survivors.title: Nav says "Pricing" while the section and command menu say "Engagements"
survivors.evidence: Navbar.tsx:18 `{ id: "pricing", label: "Pricing", hash: "#pricing" }`; Engagements.tsx:84 `eyebrow="Engagements"`; CommandMenu.tsx:112 `{ id: "pricing", label: "/pricing", hint: "Engagements", ... }`
survivors.recommendation: Change the Navbar label to "Engagements" (keep `hash: "#pricing"` so existing links work). Optionally rename the command-menu label to `/engagements`.
survivors.why_it_matters: "Pricing" in the primary nav is the first word a visitor reads that frames the site as a shop; "Engagements" frames it as a practice.

survivors.title: The process section describes the call as Day 1 but ends with no way to start it
survivors.evidence: ProcessPipeline.tsx:13 `what: "A 30-minute call on goals, constraints, and what is already breaking."` (stage 01 Discovery, line 12 `when: "Day 1"`) — correct. The stage 06 (name "Observability", not "deliver") quote `deliver: "Dashboards you can read, and an optional retainer for what comes next."` is at ProcessPipeline.tsx:54, not :56. No CTA/Link/"/book" anywhere in the file; section closes at lines 154-157. Note Audience.tsx:122's quiet CTA has no onClick/trackEvent — the tracked pattern is Navbar.tsx:192-196 (`onClick={() => trackEvent("book_call_click", { location: "navbar" })}`) and Engagements.tsx:148-153.
survivors.recommendation: Keep it to one line, not a button, to respect the brief's "reduce repeated CTAs" rule (the fixed Navbar already offers "Book an Architecture Call" on every scroll position, and Audience/Engagements two sections later carry 7 more /book links). After the in ProcessPipeline.tsx add a single Reveal-wrapped mono-tiny line: "Day 1 is a call." followed by trackEvent("book_call_click", { location: "process" })}>Book an Architecture Call (import CTA from "@/components/system/CTA" and trackEvent from "@/lib/analytics", matching Navbar.tsx:196). Do not add CTAs to Philosophy, TechMatrix or SEOFaq.
survivors.why_it_matters: This is the 60-second "I understand how he approaches architecture" moment and the copy literally names the call; a single quiet link converts understanding into the next step without adding a section.

survivors.title: Platform profile cards are rendered twice, and the Experience copy adds marketplace earnings
survivors.evidence: ProofStrip.tsx:63 `Verified on` + :64-82 external anchors to `p.url` showing `{p.status}` and `{p.rating} · {p.reviews}`; TrackRecord.tsx:114-140 same `PLATFORM_PROOF.map` as `panel panel-hover` cards with :131-133 `{p.rating} · {p.reviews} · {p.earned}` → "5.0 · 47 reviews · $50,000+" / "4.9 · 89 reviews · $30,000+"; src/data/site.ts:55,63 `earned: "$50,000+"`, `earned: "$30,000+"`
survivors.recommendation: Keep the ProofStrip links (real profiles, as the brief requires). In TrackRecord remove the duplicate platform cards (or at minimum stop rendering `earned`) and let the year log plus `CREDENTIALS` carry the section; this also stops sending mid-page traffic off-site to Upwork/Fiverr a second time.
survivors.why_it_matters: An engineering log that ends in "$50,000+ earned on Upwork" reads as a freelancer profile, and the outbound link is a second exit from the funnel in a section whose job is to build trust.

survivors.title: FAQ frames the offer as "hire a developer, available on Upwork/Fiverr" right before the close
survivors.evidence: SEOFaq.tsx:12-13 `q: "Can I hire you as a senior Laravel, PHP & MySQL developer?"` / `a: "Yes. I'm a top-rated Laravel, PHP, and MySQL developer ... I'm available on Upwork, Fiverr, or for direct hire."`; SEOFaq.tsx:28-29 `q: "What's your process for starting a new project?"` / `a: "Every engagement starts with a free 30-minute discovery call ..."` rendered as plain text with no link; SEOFaq.tsx contains no `<Link`/`<CTA` (grep)
survivors.recommendation: Rewrite Q1 as "How do engagements work?" using the Engagements lead copy, delete the "available on Upwork, Fiverr, or for direct hire" sentence, and end the Q5 answer with an inline `<Link to="/book">Book an Architecture Call</Link>`. Rebuild the section on `SectionHeader` + `Reveal` so it stops using the 60px `AnimatedSection` fade.
survivors.why_it_matters: The last block of copy before the final CTA re-labels the whole practice as a marketplace developer, and the one answer that mentions the call gives the reader nowhere to click.

survivors.title: The email capture promises a PDF that does not exist and then navigates the visitor off-site
survivors.evidence: Checklist.tsx:121 `Want it as a PDF, plus new checklists?`; Checklist.tsx:124-125 `Drop your email and I will send the printable version. No newsletter spam, only practical backend material.`; Checklist.tsx:128-129 `action="https://formspree.io/f/mkgzjlde" method="POST"` (native POST → Formspree confirmation page); Checklist.tsx:148 `Send it to me`; public/ contains no checklist PDF (only usama-munawar-cv.pdf)
survivors.recommendation: Either ship `public/laravel-scaling-checklist.pdf` and switch the form to the fetch pattern already in Contact.tsx:55-79 (stay on page, show a confirmation with the download and the architecture-call CTA), or remove the email card and let the closing "Book an Architecture Call" carry the page. The checklist content itself is on-brief and should stay.
survivors.why_it_matters: A Laravel-specific lead magnet is a good top-of-funnel for the primary specialisation, but an unfulfilled PDF promise plus a Formspree redirect burns the trust it was meant to earn.

survivors.title: Right moment, wrong label and wrong primitive on the checklist close

Swap the shadcn Button for `<CTA to="/book" size="lg" arrow>Book an Architecture Call</CTA>`, change the sentence to "Bring the list to an architecture call and leave with the shortest path to a fix.", and use `{ location: "checklist" }` to match the other book_call_click events.

survivors.title: Seven concurrent motion systems run in the hero at rest — pick two
survivors.evidence: Idle (at-rest) loops are five, not seven: SystemGraph.tsx:304 ring `rotate-slow 64s linear infinite`; SystemGraph.tsx:249-264 `anim-dash-flow` per wire (10 in wide layout, 6 in compact); Hero.tsx:150-153 scroll cue `sweep-y 2.6s ... infinite`; Hero.tsx:62 pill dot `anim-status`; Telemetry.tsx:39 status dot `anim-status`. The spotlight (Hero.tsx:47-54), magnetic CTA (CTA.tsx:83-113) and drift parallax (SystemGraph.tsx:168-169, 202, 235, 280, 329) are pointer-driven and produce no movement at rest (src/hooks/usePointerField.ts:13-14, 24, 102).
survivors.recommendation: Keep exactly two: the pointer parallax (`drift`) and the travelling dash on the wires — those are the brief's 'subtle flow, parallax, hover'. Delete the ring rotation (keep the static dashed ring and ticks), delete the scroll cue block (Hero.tsx:142-156), delete the eyebrow pill (see separate finding), keep one status dot (Telemetry 'Available for work'), and drop the spotlight layer and the magnetic CTA offset.
survivors.why_it_matters: The brief bans spinning and constant floating; a 64s rotation is still a spin, and stacking seven idle motions reads as 'award-site portfolio' rather than 'precise, cinematic'.

lows.evidence: src/components/Hero.tsx:150-153 `<span className="block h-4 w-px bg-primary/80" style={{ animation: "sweep-y 2.6s cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1) infinite" }} />` inside `className="enter pointer-events-none absolute inset-x-0 bottom-6 hidden justify-center lg:flex"` (:143); keyframes at index.css:413-418.

lows.title: Dead animation definitions shipped in CSS: marquee, pulse-node, logo-spin, slide-up, scale-in

lows.why_it_matters: Dead motion code is both bytes on every route and a temptation to reintroduce forbidden patterns later.

lows.title: Portrait and logo are served at 3× and 14× their rendered size
lows.evidence: Portrait: `src/assets/usama-profile.jpg` is 600×900 (58,358 B; header check) with a 31,996 B WebP sibling, declared `width={340} height={340}` at SystemGraph.tsx:412-413 and rendered at ≈33% of a ≤591px box (`width: `${((photo.r * 2) / vb.w) * 100}%`` :199) — i.e. ≤200px. Logo: Navbar.tsx:139-140 `width={1280} height={512}` (31,882 B VP8X WebP) rendered at `scrolled ? "h-7" : "h-8 sm:h-9"` (:143), i.e. 28–36px tall.
lows.recommendation: Export a square 400px portrait crop (2× of the largest render) as WebP inside the existing `<picture>` and add an AVIF `<source>` above it; replace the logo with an inline SVG or a 2× raster (~180×72). Keep `decoding="async"` and the `<picture>` structure.
lows.why_it_matters: ~80 KB of image for a 200px circle and a 32px wordmark is exactly the kind of thing a senior backend buyer notices in DevTools on a site that markets performance.

lows.title: CommandMenu is mounted at startup on every route, so its chunk and the dialog chunk are always fetched
lows.evidence: src/App.tsx:12 `const CommandMenu = lazy(() => import("@/components/CommandMenu"));` and :39-41 `<Suspense fallback={null}><CommandMenu /></Suspense>` outside `<Routes>`; built chunks `CommandMenu-UmQ6d4RS.js` (38,909 B) plus the dialog chunk. The keydown listener that opens it lives inside that chunk, so ⌘K does nothing until it has downloaded anyway.
lows.recommendation: Keep a ~10-line listener in App (⌘K, `/`, and the `open-command-menu` event) that flips an `open` state, and only then lazy-mount `<CommandMenu open onOpenChange>`; the palette's own code stays untouched.
lows.why_it_matters: A power-user feature should cost nothing until a power user asks for it.

lows.title: Five dependencies have zero imports and 24 more are reachable only through never-imported shadcn primitives
lows.evidence: package.json:16 `"@hookform/resolvers": "^3.9.0"`, :47 `"@vercel/analytics": "^1.5.0"`, :51 `"date-fns": "^3.6.0"`, :52 `"embla-carousel-autoplay": "^8.6.0"`, :73 `"zod": "^3.23.8"` — grep over src, vite.config.ts and tailwind.config.ts finds 0 imports of each; :46 `"@types/react-syntax-highlighter"` sits under `dependencies`. Only 20 of the 49 files in src/components/ui are imported outside ui/ (grep list: accordion, avatar, badge, button, card, command, dialog, input, label, separator, sheet, skeleton, sonner, tabs, textarea, toast, toaster, toggle, tooltip, use-toast), leaving recharts, vaul, react-day-picker, react-hook-form, react-resizable-panels, input-otp, embla-carousel-react and 17 @radix-ui packages installed for nothing.

No runtime bundle change (tree-shaken already) but a much smaller install and lockfile — 'no dependency bloat' per the brief.
lows.why_it_matters: A hiring engineer who opens package.json sees a chart library, a carousel autoplayer and a form validator on a portfolio with no charts, carousels or validated forms.

lows.title: Between 1024 and 1279px the header shows a hamburger, a ⌘K pill and the full-label CTA but no inline links
lows.evidence:
src/components/Navbar.tsx:149 `
    `; :208 hamburger `... xl:hidden"`; :185 ⌘K `... lg:inline-flex"`; :198 `Book an Architecture Call`. So at the 1024 test width a laptop reader gets a phone-style menu next to desktop-only affordances.
lows.recommendation: Show the link list from `lg` and defer the ⌘K pill to `xl` (it is the least valuable of the three at that width); the eight 13.5px links plus logo and CTA fit a 960px container.
lows.why_it_matters: 1024 is a named test width and is the first width where the site otherwise composes as 'desktop'.

lows.title: Hovering the principle list rewrites an `aria-live` region and the buttons are marked `aria-pressed` toggles
lows.evidence: src/components/Philosophy.tsx:122-125 `onClick={() => setActive(i)} onMouseEnter={() => setActive(i)} onFocus={() => setActive(i)} aria-pressed={on}`; :163 `<div className="min-h-[7rem] pt-7" aria-live="polite">` wraps the body that changes with every hover.
lows.recommendation: Drop `onMouseEnter` (click/focus is enough for a five-item list), remove `aria-live` (this is content selection, not a status message), and use `aria-current="true"` on the selected principle instead of `aria-pressed`.
lows.why_it_matters: A screen-reader user with a trackpad gets the body text re-announced every time the pointer wanders; the semantics say 'toggle button' for what is really a selection.

lows.title: `role="tablist"/"tab"` is declared without panels, `aria-controls` or arrow-key navigation
lows.evidence: src/components/TechMatrix.tsx:126-128 `role="tablist" aria-label="Technology categories" className="scroll-x no-scrollbar -mx-1 flex max-w-full gap-1 px-1"`; :135-136 `role="tab" aria-selected={on}` with no `id`/`aria-controls`/`tabIndex` handling; no `role="tabpanel"` anywhere in the file; :210 the detail panel is `aria-live="polite"` instead.
lows.recommendation: Either complete the ARIA tabs pattern (ids, `aria-controls`, `role="tabpanel"`, Left/Right key handling) or — simpler and honest — drop the tab roles and use plain buttons with `aria-pressed`. Keep the `scroll-x` strip; it is the right mobile treatment.
lows.why_it_matters: Half-implemented ARIA is worse than none: assistive tech announces a tab widget whose keyboard contract then fails.

lows.title: The ⌘K dialog has no accessible name
lows.evidence: src/components/ui/command.tsx:28-33 `<Dialog {...props}><DialogContent className="overflow-hidden p-0 shadow-lg"><Command className=...>{children}</Command></DialogContent></Dialog>` renders no `DialogTitle`; CommandMenu.tsx:167 supplies only the input placeholder `Jump to a section, page, or action…`. Radix Dialog warns in the console for exactly this.
lows.recommendation: Add a visually hidden `<DialogTitle className="sr-only">Command menu</DialogTitle>` (and a matching `DialogDescription`) inside CommandDialog — two lines, no new dependency.
lows.why_it_matters: A console warning on ⌘K and an unnamed modal are both visible to the senior engineer the site is trying to impress.

lows.section: Small controls (CTA size=sm, footer socials, TechMatrix tabs, chatbot close)
lows.title: Several touch targets are 32–36px tall on mobile
lows.evidence: src/components/system/CTA.tsx:55 `sm: "h-9 px-4 text-[13px] gap-1.5",` used at Audience.tsx:122 `<CTA to="/book" tone="quiet" size="sm" arrow className="px-0">` (36px, horizontal padding removed) and Contact.tsx:145/:333; Footer.tsx:50 `className="flex h-9 w-9 items-center justify-center rounded-full ..."` (36px); TechMatrix.tsx:142 `rounded-full border px-3.5 py-2 font-inter text-[13px]` (~34px); AIChatbot.tsx:284 `className="text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary-foreground/20 h-8 w-8"` (32px).

lows.title: A fully styled, differently-worded fallback page paints inside #root and is then replaced by React
lows.evidence:
index.html:219-223 `
...

Usama Munawar — Backend Systems Engineer for Laravel, VoIP & AI

`, while the React hero renders `Production-grade backend, engineered.` (Hero.tsx:73-78); src/main.tsx:20 `createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(` swaps the whole subtree.

lows.title: The evidence tags under each headline number only appear on hover, so touch users never see them
lows.evidence:
src/components/ProofStrip.tsx:47-49 `

{m.note}

` — the notes are the sourcing labels from src/data/site.ts (`"Upwork · Fiverr · direct"`, `"Lifetime earnings"`).
lows.recommendation: Show the note always (drop `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100`); it is one 11px line per cell and it is the part that connects a number to its evidence — exactly what the credibility phase asks for.

lows.title: Every page preconnects to images.unsplash.com although no landing-page image is hosted there
lows.evidence: index.html:46-47 `<link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://images.unsplash.com" /> <link rel="preconnect" href="https://images.unsplash.com" crossorigin />`; Unsplash URLs exist only as `featured_image` values on some blog posts in src/data/blogs.ts (and on /projects), never in Hero, CaseStudies (local WebPs at CaseStudies.tsx:110 `src={study.image}`) or Insights' local assets.

lows.title: Keyword meta, blanket hreflang, Speakable schema and a 'hand-crafted' self-declaration add noise and one contradiction
lows.evidence: index.html:59 `<meta name="keywords" content="… ai engineer, claude developer, … full stack developer pakistan" />`; index.html:62-63 `hreflang="en"` and `"x-default"` both → `https://dev-usama-portfolio.vercel.app/` on every SPA route; index.html:206-209 `"speakable": { … "cssSelector": ["h1", "h2", ".speakable", "[data-speakable]"] }` (no such class/attribute in src); index.html:214-215 `<meta name="ai-content-declaration" content="human-authored" />` / `<meta name="generator" content="Hand-crafted by Usama Munawar" />` while src/main.tsx:12 redirects from `usama-showcase-sparkle.lovable.app`

lows.title: Declared og:image size does not match the file, and per-route previews declare no size at all

lows.title: Article titles are cut at 55 characters with an ellipsis before they reach the SERP

lows.title: Three phrasings of 'available' and four hand-maintained sameAs lists that already disagree about X

lows.evidence: src/components/Navbar.tsx:14 `label: "Work"`, :18 `label: "Pricing"`, :12 `label: "About"`; src/components/Engagements.tsx:84 `eyebrow="Engagements"`; src/components/CommandMenu.tsx:112 hint `Engagements`

refuted.title: 'Is this you?' is the 20-second 'systems like mine' moment but sits seventh, after process and track record
refuted.reason:
The cited evidence is accurate (d:\Usama Portfolio\src\components\Audience.tsx:19, :21, :37, :87 index="07"; d:\Usama Portfolio\src\pages\Index.tsx:136), but the recommendation conflicts with the owner brief and the finding misdescribes what the section renders.

1. Brief hierarchy conflict. The brief orders L1 who I am + what I solve → L2 proof → L3 case studies → L4 architecture → L5 services, and states "Case studies carry credibility." Audience is a "Who I work with" persona/diagnosis section (its own doc comment, Audience.tsx:71; eyebrow at :88) whose panels are "The problem / What I do about it" — services-adjacent content ("Services explain problems solved"), not an L1 layer; the brief has no persona slot at L1. Moving it to directly after ProofStrip would make the page Hero → ProofStrip → Audience → ServiceExplorer → CaseStudies, pushing the L3 case studies (CaseStudies.tsx:192, index "03") to fifth position behind two services-flavoured sections. That directly contradicts L2 → L3 → L5 and the "case studies carry credibility" rule.

2. "What I solve" is not missing from L1. The Hero already states it in the first scroll: eyebrow "Backend systems · AI · Automation · VoIP" (Hero.tsx:64-66) and the lead "I architect and ship scalable Laravel systems, automation infrastructure, real-time platforms, and AI-powered backends for teams that need software to work in production." (Hero.tsx:90-92). ServiceExplorer ("What I build", index "02", ServiceExplorer.tsx:182-183) already sits directly after ProofStrip (Index.tsx:127-130) and names the seven systems (Laravel & Backend, SaaS & API, AI & Agent…). Inserting a second, longer "what I solve" block there duplicates content, which the brief forbids ("do not add more; consolidate duplicates; reduce repeated … service blurbs").

3. The brief's 20-second beat is "he has WORKED ON systems like mine" — an evidence beat served by the real case studies at 03, not by self-declared target personas. The recommendation would push the very section that delivers that beat further down the page.

4. The finding treats Audience as "the four panels" only, but the same section also renders the three named testimonials (Audience.tsx:46-68, "Client feedback" block at :131-161). "Move Audience directly after ProofStrip" would silently relocate the testimonials above the case studies as well; the finding does not account for this.

Audience's current slot (07, between TrackRecord 06 and Engagements 08) is a coherent conversion bridge: diagnosis ("If one of these is uncomfortably familiar, we should talk", :90) → engagement models → FinalCTA/Contact, matching L6 → L7 → L8.

The one defensible part of the recommendation — collapsing the four per-panel "Talk through this" CTAs (Audience.tsx:121-125, rendered once per panel) into a single CTA — aligns with the brief's "reduce repeated CTAs" and can be done without moving the section.
